_comment: The Potato Council's roster. Talent is 0-10 and RELATIVE: a prior for routing, not a benchmark. Resolution: this file, then ~/.claude/astrafabulopus/models.json, then the project's .claude/orchestra/models.json, merged per model and per talent, so an overlay can re-rate one talent without restating a model. When a model ships: `af-council add NEW --like NEAREST --bump dim=+1`, then `af-tryout NEW` for observed numbers. Prices are API list $ per 1M tokens (input/cached/output); a subscription absorbs them, but they predict how fast a window drains. Priors last rated 2026-09-27 from the sources in each model's evidence list.

dimensions.architecture: Judgment the spec cannot capture: decomposition, interfaces, trade-offs, knowing what not to build.
dimensions.implementation: Turning a complete six-part spec into correct, minimal code on the first try.
dimensions.debugging: Hard bugs: concurrency, algorithms, flaky tests, the ones that resisted a first attempt.
dimensions.review: Finding the real problem in a diff and giving a calibrated ship / fix-first / rethink.
dimensions.speed: Turnaround for a typical lane run.
dimensions.efficiency: Useful work per unit of budget: price times verbosity. 10 = barely dents a window.

scoring._comment: budget_reserve: the architect lives on the Claude subscription, so spending it on lane work costs a little extra. diversity_bonus: credit for a different vendor than the architect on complex, frontier, review and consult work, because a reviewer from the same family shares its blind spots.

routine.about: The spec fully determines the outcome: wiring, CRUD, tests mirroring a pattern, docs.

mechanical.about: Renames, formatting, doc edits nobody is waiting on.

complex.about: Judgment the spec cannot capture: concurrency, algorithms, security paths, hard debugging.

frontier.about: The hardest one-off, after two strong attempts failed.

review.about: Reading a diff against the goal and returning ship / fix-first / rethink.

consult.about: A second opinion on an expensive-to-reverse decision.

architect.about: The session model: all-day judgment, specs and verdicts.

claude-opus-5-5.name: Opus 5.5
claude-opus-5-5.spud: Yukon Gold. Buttery, versatile, excellent at nearly everything. Suspiciously so. Was not allowed to vote on its own scores. Tried anyway.
claude-opus-5-5.notes: Anthropic: 'performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work', 40% cheaper and 30% faster than Opus 5, about half the tokens on a command-line benchmark. Adaptive thinking is always on. The default architect and the Claude build lane.

claude-fable-5-1.name: Fable 5.1
claude-fable-5-1.spud: Heirloom Purple Peruvian. Rare, expensive, profound. Served once, at the end of the meal: the final review.
claude-fable-5-1.notes: Mythos-tier with extra safeguards; 'demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work' (Slower). Behind Opus 5.5 on the coding benchmarks Anthropic published, kept as the final reviewer for its clean-context judgment.

claude-sonnet-5.name: Sonnet 5
claude-sonnet-5.spud: Russet. The dependable workhorse. Bakes, fries, mashes, never complains. Runs the lane wrappers and the verifier.
claude-sonnet-5.notes: 'Best combination of speed and intelligence' (Fast). $2/$10 made permanent. A Sonnet 5.5 is reportedly coming.

claude-haiku-4-5.name: Haiku 4.5
claude-haiku-4-5.spud: Fingerling. Tiny, fast, elegant, and retiring soon. Pour one out.
claude-haiku-4-5.notes: Retirement 'not sooner than October 15, 2026'. No effort levels (extended thinking instead). A Haiku 5.5 is reportedly coming.

gpt-6-astra.name: GPT-6 Astra
gpt-6-astra.spud: Sweet potato. Brilliant, expensive, and not technically a potato at all. The Council tolerates it. Barely. IT'S RIGHT THERE IN THE NAME.
gpt-6-astra.notes: OpenAI's 'most capable model, built for the hardest end-to-end work'. About 65% fewer output tokens than Opus 5, which softens the price. The occasional frontier lane and the cross-vendor second advisor.

gpt-6-sol.name: GPT-6 Sol
gpt-6-sol.spud: Red Bliss. Firm under heat, holds its shape in a hard stew. The escalation you can afford.
gpt-6-sol.notes: 'Built to power complex coding and agentic workflows'; reportedly about half the mistakes of its predecessor. ultra is slow and adds Codex's own delegation: save it for twice-resisted problems.

gpt-6-luna.name: GPT-6 Luna
gpt-6-luna.spud: Tater Tot. Small, fast, absurdly cheap, and far better than it has any right to be. Never underestimate the tot.
gpt-6-luna.notes: 'Most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks'. Output is about 100x cheaper than Astra's. The default routine lane. OpenAI's guide lists ultra for Luna; fable-advisor reports Codex rejects it, so it is left out here.
evidence: created a file through the lane in 14 s (astrafabulopus day one, as GPT-5.6 Luna)

gpt-5.6-sol.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
gpt-5.6-sol.spud: Last season's Red Bliss. Still good in a stew; costs more than the new crop.
gpt-5.6-sol.notes: Fallback if a login rejects the GPT-6 slugs (Codex 0.154 did; `codex update` fixed it).

gpt-5.6-terra.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
gpt-5.6-terra.spud: Maris Piper. A solid middle-of-the-sack spud. Nobody's favorite, nobody's regret.

gpt-5.6-luna.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
gpt-5.6-luna.spud: The frozen tot. The old tot. Fine in a pinch, and it was there for us.

qwen3.6-27b-mlx.name: Qwen 3.6 27B
qwen3.6-27b-mlx.spud: Garden potato. Grown at home, costs nothing, slow to harvest. Smells like soil and freedom.
qwen3.6-27b-mlx.notes: Through LM Studio via Codex's built-in provider. Local buys cost, not speed: 195 s for a task Luna did in 14 s on day one. Never run it during a build.
evidence: SWE-bench Verified 77.2 as reported by Qwen (huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B), far slower on a laptop than any hosted lane
